buyerGuides.title: How to Read Japanese Auction Sheets (USS, TAA, CAA)
buyerGuides.summary: Understand Japanese auction ratings: Grade S (brand new), Grade 5 (pristine/as new), Grade 4.5 (excellent), Grade 4 (good), and interior grades A to C.
keyPoints: Grade 5 & 4.5 represent the top 10% condition among Japanese vehicles.
Interior Grade A indicates smoke-free, tear-free upholstery with original scent.
Look for the inspector's diagram in the bottom right for any cosmetic panel markings (A1 = light scratch, U1 = minor dimple).

buyerGuides.title: Recon vs Local Used: What Are the Real Differences?
buyerGuides.summary: Recon vehicles are imported from Japan without prior registration in Malaysia, qualifying for lower bank interest rates and fresh road wear.
keyPoints: Recon cars qualify for new/recon hire purchase rates (approx 2.30% - 2.80% p.a.), significantly lower than local used car rates (3.5% - 4.2%).
Japanese roads are exceptionally smooth and salt-controlled in central regions, preserving chassis bushing integrity.
Strict Japanese shaken vehicle inspections mandate regular maintenance and fluid renewals.

buyerGuides.title: Approved Permits (AP), Customs Duty & Legality in Malaysia
buyerGuides.summary: Everything you need to know about Approved Permits (AP), Royal Malaysian Customs K1 clearance forms, and JPJ registration safety.
keyPoints: A genuine AP is required by MITI for every imported recon vehicle into Malaysia.
Always request to sight the Customs K1 Form confirming full duties have been settled.
PUSPAKOM B5/B7 inspection ensures vehicle chassis and engine numbers match factory records.
